assertions.name: the_block_gram_is_singular_and_its_radical_is_the_alternating_block
assertions.source: exactly one diagonal entry vanishes, at (1, 1, 1). nucleus_sdp_assembly.CostGram.gram IS np.diag(frob_diag) with frob_diag = y_lambda * dim_lambda, so the Gram is diagonal and its radical is the coordinate direction v = (0, 0, 1). Under convention D y_(1^3) = 0 -- that vanishing IS convention D (threeRow_eq_zero_of_jones_ocneanu; converse is markovWeights_eq_jones_of_threeRow_eq_zero + hfaith) -- so the singularity is structural, not a numerical rank drop

assertions.name: the_radical_pairing_hypothesis_holds
assertions.source: <1, v> = 1.0 != 0, so dual_price_determined_by_radical applies and y_0 is FORCED to <t, v> / <1, v>. Checked rather than assumed, because that theorem carries it as a hypothesis and it is a fact about this basis, not about every Gram

assertions.name: the_geometric_cost_is_orthogonal_to_the_radical_STRUCTURALLY
assertions.source: <t, v> = t_(1^3) = 0 for every candidate, and it is zero BY CONSTRUCTION rather than numerically: t_lambda = y_lambda * (pair sum) carries the same y_lambda factor that makes the Gram diagonal entry vanish. Two separate things kill this block, and the printout above separates them: the raw chi_(1^3) pair sums are LARGE (~15.32), so the geometry there is not degenerate and it is the WEIGHT that zeroes the cost -- but they are also IDENTICAL across all four candidates, so the alternating block carries no discriminating information either and would contribute none even if y_(1^3) were nonzero. The weight argument is the structural one and holds for ANY cost of the form t_lambda = y_lambda * f(lambda), for any f whatsoever, so no choice of geometric energy escapes it

assertions.name: therefore_the_shadow_price_collapses_exactly_as_the_hecke_cost_does
assertions.source: y_0 = 0 for every candidate, by ECatLPDualRadical.dual_price_zero_of_cost_orthogonal_to_radical. So the geometric cost does NOT escape the degeneracy on the block basis -- it reaches the same collapse the Hecke cost reaches, by a different route. This is a scope-(b) STRUCTURAL exclusion and the invariant is named: the shared y_lambda factor between the Gram diagonal and the cost. Reported as found; no alternative basis was substituted to obtain a better answer

assertions.name: the_operator_basis_program_is_NOT_touched_by_this
assertions.source: the corpus's other operator-selection program runs on the H_3 SIX-OPERATOR basis (gamma, sigma_0, sigma_1, L+, L-, e^-) with a DENSE Gram G_ij = tr_M(b_i b_j) whose radical is the q-antisymmetriser (-q^3, q^2, q^2, -q, -q, 1). That is a different index space and the per-block cost is not a vector in it, so nothing here bears on it. The route therefore survives only as 'build the geometric cost on the OPERATOR basis' -- an energy per operator rather than per block, which does not exist yet. Recorded as an assertion so the surviving form travels with the negative

description: The two-number measurement ECatLPDualRadical licensed, and it is a NEGATIVE. On the block basis the corpus Gram is diagonal, diag(y_lambda * dim_lambda), so under convention D (y_(1^3) = 0) its radical is the (1^3) coordinate direction. The discretised-E_cat cost carries the SAME y_lambda factor, so its (1^3) component is zero too and <t, v> = 0 identically -- not numerically small, structurally zero. By dual_price_zero_of_cost_orthogonal_to_radical the shadow price y_0 = 0, the same collapse the Hecke cost suffers. Scope-(b) for ANY cost of the form t_lambda = y_lambda * f(lambda), for any f. It does NOT touch the six-OPERATOR-basis program, whose radical is the q-antisymmetriser in a different index space; a geometric cost there is a different construction that does not exist yet.

verdict.invariant: the shared y_lambda factor: t_lambda = y_lambda * f(lambda) is orthogonal to the radical of diag(y_lambda * dim_lambda) for every f
verdict.excluded: any y_lambda-weighted per-block cost, on the block basis
verdict.NOT_excluded: a geometric cost on the six-operator basis, whose radical is the q-antisymmetriser -- a different index space, and a construction that does not exist yet
